findings.claim: The minute table does not demonstrate that required content and activities fit the frozen calendar blocks. It compares only topic-page budgets with each day's full 120-minute capacity while omitting the other fixed activities and the planned labs/projects. For example, FT12 assigns 90 minutes of topic pages even though the Fast template reserves only 10 minutes for Skim and reserves the other 110 minutes for warm-up, diagnostic, project, timed work and reflection; S21 and S26 similarly have fixed 120-minute Lab templates before the planned page minutes are accounted for. The statement that all planned totals fit is therefore not supported by a complete learner schedule.

evidence.section: dayTypes.Fast, dayTypes.Lab, dayTypes.Project and tracks S21, S26, S27, FT12-FT15

findings.recommendation: Keep every frozen topic and day block. Before authoring, replace the capacity-only table with a per-day block allocation that says which page, quiz, video, lab or project activity fulfills each fixed block; give each planned lab its duration; and count an artifact either inside a named block or as additional time, never both or neither. For Fast days, state how the canonical pages support the 10-minute skim and 70-minute direct project without implying that all page budgets can consume the same 120-minute pool. Escalate any honest overflow rather than compressing objectives or learner time.

findings.claim: Objective o1 is a real-tool performance (scaffold a Vite project and start its server), but the applicability decision says a simulated page terminal supplies the practice and points only to a later npm ci setup. A simulator can rehearse command choice, but it cannot establish that the learner created a project, started a server and recognized successful output. As written, the declared objective is not aligned to an authentic check.

evidence.section: Getting Started: Scaffolding Your First Vite Project and starting the development server

findings.recommendation: Keep the frozen project-setup topic. Map o1 to an explicit authentic learner-side step: either a small Standard real-tool lab, or a named step in the S27 project with an equivalent Fast direct-project step. Let the page simulator prepare learners and check command reasoning, but do not claim it verifies successful scaffolding/server startup. If authentic performance is deferred to the project, state that in the objective-to-activity map and use a narrower page-level objective for the in-page check.

findings.claim: All three objectives require operating an actual DevTools debugger—setting line and conditional breakpoints, stepping, watching values and locating a fault—yet the topic records no lab because page simulators will carry the practice. A simulated debugger can support prediction and explanation, but it cannot provide evidence that the learner can find the real controls and debug real executing code. The omission reason therefore does not satisfy the stated objectives.

evidence.section: Pause your code with breakpoints: line-of-code and conditional breakpoints

findings.recommendation: Keep the frozen DevTools topic. Add an authentic local-browser exercise using a small buggy HTML/JS file and real Chrome or Firefox DevTools, with a language-native public test for the repaired behavior if it is packaged as a Standard lab; map Fast learners to the equivalent debugging step in direct project implementation. The page simulator may scaffold the workflow, but the check for these objectives must require the real tool. Alternatively, distinguish simulator-level trace objectives from the later real-tool performance instead of claiming the simulator completes both.
